title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Civil Mediation by People's Courts

articles.content_en:
According to the provisions of Article 95 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court may invite enterprises, institutions, social organizations or other organizations that have a specific relationship with the parties or have certain connections with the case, and individuals who have specialized knowledge, specific social experience, a specific relationship with the parties, and who are conducive to facilitating mediation, to assist in the mediation work.
With the consent of all parties, the People's Court may entrust the units or individuals specified in the preceding paragraph to mediate the case. After a mediation agreement is reached, the People's Court shall confirm it according to law.

If the parties reach a settlement agreement on their own during the litigation, the People's Court may, upon the application of the parties, confirm the settlement agreement according to law and prepare a mediation document. The period during which both parties apply for out-of-court settlement shall not be counted into the trial period.
If, during the settlement process, the parties apply to the People's Court for coordination of the settlement activities, the People's Court may assign judicial support personnel or invite or entrust relevant units or individuals to engage in coordination activities.

The People's Court shall, before mediation, inform the parties of the names of the personnel presiding over the mediation and the clerk, and of the relevant litigation rights and obligations, such as whether to apply for withdrawal.

Where the People's Court mediates a case before the expiration of the defense period, if no mediation agreement is reached within 15 days from the date on which the parties agree to mediation for cases subject to ordinary procedure, or within 7 days from the date on which the parties agree to mediation for cases subject to summary procedure, the mediation may continue upon the consent of all parties. The extended mediation period shall not be counted into the trial period.

Where a party applies for mediation not to be conducted in public, the People's Court shall permit it.
During mediation, all parties shall be present at the same time; where necessary, mediation work may also be conducted with the parties separately.
The parties may propose a mediation plan on their own, and the persons presiding over the mediation may also propose a mediation plan for reference during the consultation of the parties.
Where the content of the mediation agreement exceeds the claims of the litigation, the People's Court may permit it.

The People's Court shall permit a mediation agreement that stipulates that a party who fails to perform the agreement shall bear civil liability.
Where a mediation agreement contains a clause stipulating that if one party fails to perform the agreement, the other party may request the People's Court to render a judgment on the case, the People's Court shall not permit it.

Where a mediation agreement stipulates that one party provides a guarantee, or a non-party agrees to provide a guarantee for the parties, the People's Court shall permit it.
Where a non-party provides a guarantee, the People's Court shall, when preparing the mediation document, list the guarantor and deliver the mediation document to the guarantor. If the guarantor does not sign for receipt of the mediation document, it shall not affect the validity of the mediation document.
The guarantee provided by a party or a non-party shall take effect when it meets the conditions prescribed by the Civil Code.

If the parties cannot reach an agreement on the apportionment of litigation costs, it shall not affect the validity of the mediation agreement. The People's Court may directly decide the proportions of litigation costs to be borne by the parties and record the decision in the mediation document.

Where a party who neither enjoys rights nor bears obligations under the content of the mediation document fails to sign for receipt of the mediation document, it shall not affect the validity of the mediation document.

Where a party raises an objection on the ground that the civil mediation document is inconsistent with the original intent of the mediation agreement, and the People's Court, after review, considers the objection to be justified, it shall, in accordance with the mediation agreement, make a ruling to correct the relevant content of the civil mediation document.

Where the parties reach a mediation agreement on part of the litigation claims, the People's Court may confirm it first and prepare a mediation document.
Where the parties reach a mediation agreement on the main litigation claims and request the People's Court to propose handling opinions on the litigation claims for which no agreement has been reached and indicate that they accept the handling results, the handling opinions of the People's Court are part of the mediation agreement; when a mediation document is prepared, they shall be recorded in the mediation document.

When the conditions of the guarantee clause or the conditions for bearing civil liability determined in the mediation document are fulfilled, if the parties apply for enforcement, the People's Court shall enforce in accordance with law.
After a party who fails to perform the mediation agreement has borne the civil liability determined in the mediation document in accordance with the preceding paragraph, if the other party further requests it to bear the liability for delayed performance provided in Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall not support the request.

Where a mediation document stipulates the delivery of a specific subject matter, the real rights and priority rights of a third party that already existed on the property before the mediation agreement was reached shall not be affected. If a third party raises an objection to the subject matter of enforcement during enforcement, it shall be handled in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law.
Where the People's Court conducts mediation in cases of incidental civil actions in criminal proceedings, these Provisions shall apply.

Cases that have been accepted by the People's Court before the implementation of these Provisions and have not yet been finally concluded after these Provisions come into force shall be handled in accordance with these Provisions.
Where the relevant judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court made before the implementation of these Provisions are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall apply.

These Provisions shall come into force as of November 1, 2004.
